controversy.en: Development frozen (2025) as the company pivots to the Dia AI browser; past CVE let attackers hijack sessions via a user ID; security team grew from 1 to 5.

data.en: Account-based sync through The Browser Company servers; AI features send page content to their models.

controversy.en: Same parent as Opera: China's Kunlun Tech holds ~72%. The famous CPU/RAM limiters are mostly cosmetic; Hindenburg allegations apply to the group.

data.en: Same as Opera: browsing data on Opera servers; free VPN via Opera infrastructure.

controversy.en: No major scandals. Co-developed with the Tor Project (2023); Mullvad VPN famously refused police access requests.

data.en: None: no telemetry, no identifiers, anti-fingerprinting on by default.

controversy.en: Unofficial Chromium builds by one developer; optimized for AVX2 CPUs; no reproducible-builds guarantee, so you trust the maintainer.

data.en: Same as Chromium minus several Google services and background requests.

controversy.en: Japanese project that was closed-source for years despite using Firefox; opened its code in 2023. Governance is community-driven but small.

data.en: Telemetry disabled by default; a few features contact Japanese project servers.

controversy.en: Sold to ad company System1 (2020); founder Alex Kontos bought independence back (2023). No scandals since.

data.en: Telemetry removed; monetization via partner search engines only.

controversy.en: No scandals; the trade-off is manual update checking and occasional site breakage from aggressive removal of Google dependencies.

data.en: No Google connections by design; no telemetry; web searches depend on your chosen engine.

controversy.en: Arc's successor, invite beta; the AI reads page content and chat history to act on your behalf; no independent security audit yet.

data.en: Page content and conversations are sent to The Browser Company AI models; account required.

controversy.en: Parent Avast was caught selling browsing histories via subsidiary Jumpshot (shut down 2020; $16.5M FTC settlement 2024); browser is pushed hard by Avast antivirus.

data.en: Avast telemetry and promotional offers; given the parent's record, assume profiling unless proven otherwise.

controversy.en: No major scandals. Only gripe: security patches can lag Firefox release days slightly while the community rebuilds.

data.en: None by default: telemetry, Pocket, Google services and data collection removed at build time.

controversy.en: Mozilla earns most revenue from the Google default deal; telemetry on by default; 2025 ToS briefly implied a broad data license (rolled back after backlash).

data.en: Telemetry, crash reports and location-based suggestions; privacy-preserving ad measurement (PPA) experiments.

controversy.en: Owned ~72% by China's Kunlun Tech (SEC filings). Hindenburg Research alleged its fintech apps charged 365-876% APR loans. VPN audited by Deloitte (no-log).

data.en: Browsing data processed on Opera servers; free VPN routes traffic through Opera infrastructure.

controversy.en: Owned by Korean internet giant Naver; subject to South Korean data law; sidebar services (translate, shopping) phone home to Naver.

data.en: Naver account sync, usage telemetry to Naver servers; personalization tied to Naver services.

controversy.en: Closed source; the Windows port is young and rough. Kagi's paid search model is the business — privacy as a product, not surveillance.

data.en: Zero telemetry claimed; no ad profiles; sync on Apple via iCloud, local on Windows.

controversy.en: Ancient Goanna engine misses years of Chromium/Firefox security mitigations; site breakage is common; one-maintainer project.

data.en: Low telemetry, but the outdated engine itself is the bigger risk.

controversy.en: Ships affiliate bookmarks and monetizes default search (Google affiliate); UI is closed-source even though the Chromium core is open. Dec 2024: secretly enabled ad attribution scripts on partner search engines for revenue. Norwegian company, no profiling.

data.en: No profiling; end-to-end encrypted sync; usage stats only if you opt in.

controversy.en: Used for both censorship circumvention and darknet markets (Silk Road); exit nodes can see non-HTTPS traffic; blocked or flagged by some governments and sites.

data.en: Traffic hops through 3 encrypted volunteer relays; no telemetry; log into personal accounts and you break your own anonymity.

controversy.en: Young project with a tiny team; no independent security audit yet. Fast-moving releases can introduce regressions.

data.en: Firefox-based with telemetry off; updates flow through Mozilla infrastructure.

controversy.en: Sends unique device IDs even with telemetry off; aggressive Bing sidebar ads, sponsored suggestions and persistent switch-back prompts.

data.en: Diagnostic data, browsing history when sync is on, advertising ID for personalized ads.

controversy.en: QtWebEngine (Chromium core) security patches lag upstream; small KDE team; Windows builds less battle-tested than the Linux ones.

data.en: Minimal telemetry; KDE desktop integration only if you use those services.

controversy.en: Closed source despite privacy claims: the tracker blocklist and data handling cannot be independently audited.

data.en: Claims no telemetry and blocks trackers aggressively; unverifiable due to closed code.

controversy.en: Russian jurisdiction: data laws allow state access (SORM); Turbo mode proxies pages through Yandex servers; Alice assistant processes voice in Russia.

data.en: Extensive telemetry, search, location and voice data to Yandex (Russia); personalized ads.

controversy.en: Antitrust case: DOJ won remedies (Sept 2025) — Google must share search data with rivals, no exclusive default deals. Incognito tracking lawsuit ended with deletion of billions of records. Privacy Sandbox keeps ad profiling in-house.

data.en: Syncs history, searches, location and voice to your Google account; ad personalization by default.

controversy.en: 2020: auto-added affiliate codes to crypto exchange URLs (CEO apologized). Founder Brendan Eich's Prop-8 donation past resurfaces periodically. Otherwise strong privacy record.

data.en: Minimal by design: P3A privacy-preserving stats (can disable), no search or profile tracking.

controversy.en: Shows as managed by your organization.

data.en: Turns off extras and telemetry.

controversy.en: Shows as managed by your organization.

data.en: Turns off shopping, extras and telemetry.

controversy.en: Perplexity's AI browser: page content is sent to AI models; Cloudflare accused it of aggressive scraping (2025); agentic browsing raises new privacy questions.

data.en: Browsing context processed by Perplexity AI; account required; search history tied to your Perplexity profile.

controversy.en: 2022: its browser let Microsoft trackers through due to a Bing syndication deal (researcher Zach Edwards exposed it); patched August 2022.

data.en: No ad profiles; search keeps anonymous logs; browser sync is encrypted.

controversy.en: No auto-updater on Windows builds: security fixes depend on whoever compiles your binary (Hibbiki, etc.); some Google APIs (sync) removed.

data.en: Chrome engine without Google sync and services; web searches depend on the engine you pick.

controversy.en: Niche build by the CachyOS (Arch) community; requires AVX2; tiny review surface, so fewer eyes on the code than mainstream browsers.

data.en: Chromium-based with minimal documented patches; telemetry follows upstream Chromium defaults minus Google services.
